label: prop:hecke-generator-poly-reduction
title: Single-generator Hecke polynomial reduction
html:
Proposition. Single-generator Hecke polynomial reduction

Let \sigma_i be a Hecke generator, satisfying the quadratic relation \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\,\sigma_i + 1. For any finite list of scalars d_1, \dots, d_r \in R, the product of single-generator factors collapses to an R-linear combination of \sigma_i and the identity,

  \prod_{j=1}^{r} \bigl(\sigma_i + d_j\,1\bigr) \;=\; \alpha\,\sigma_i + \beta\,1,

where (\alpha, \beta) is given by the division-free recursion

  (\alpha,\beta)_{\varnothing} = (0,\,1),
  \qquad
  (\alpha,\beta)_{d\,::\,\mathrm{ds}}
    = \bigl(\alpha'\,(h + d) + \beta',\;\; \alpha' + \beta'\,d\bigr),

with h = q - q^{-1} and (\alpha',\beta') the coefficients for the tail \mathrm{ds}.

Consequence for the Markov trace

In a seminormal (Gelfand–Zetlin) representation the diagonal entry of \alpha\,\sigma_i + \beta\,1 on a two-box block depends only on the content gap \delta' of the two boxes added at that step, through the eigenvalue D(\delta') of \sigma_i. Hence whenever a braid word has a monotone generator sequence — as the multi-nucleon atom word \beta_{\mathrm{atom}} does, each nucleon contributing \sigma_{3k}, \sigma_{3k+1} and one interface crossing \sigma_{3k+2} without revisiting a generator — every per-generator operator O_g is a single-generator polynomial, and its seminormal diagonal is a single \alpha_g\,D(\delta'_g) + \beta_g. The character then factorises as a sum over Bratteli chains of a product of such local factors:

  \chi^\lambda(\beta_{\mathrm{atom}})
   = \sum_{\varnothing = s_0 \subset s_1 \subset \cdots \subset s_n = \lambda}
       \ \prod_g \bigl(\alpha_g\,D(\delta'_g) + \beta_g\bigr),

a transfer matrix over the Young lattice that never materialises the d_\lambda-dimensional Hoefsmit representation. This is the mechanism by which the canonical Markov trace \mathrm{tr}_M = \sum_\lambda y_\lambda\,\chi^\lambda scales to large atoms (Steps 3 and 9b of the mass–binding chain): the per-block work drops to a few field operations, removing the n! wall of the per-basis-vector evaluation.
